title: Deploy a scissor boom at 1 g, carrying its tip by its offload sling
instruction: Deploy the white scissor boom to its latched full length, handling it only by its black sling and keeping its tip at least 1 cm above the blue solar cells, then let go.
context: Aerospace engineering and operations technicians (O*NET 17-3021) and aircraft structure and systems assemblers (51-2011) run 1 g deployment checks of booms and antennas before flight. Flight hinges are sized for zero g, so on the ground an offload carriage takes the moving end's weight by a cable that must hang vertical, since a tilted cable side-loads the boom's pins, while the drive extends it; the hardware is handled only at its ground-support points. Here a hand crank drives a self-locking screw that opens a two-bay scissor boom 173 mm, its tip running out about 5 times faster per turn early in the stroke than late. Unsupported, the boom sags past its root hinge's 3 deg rating and onto the solar cells, whose keep-out is 10 mm, and the root latch engages only with the boom level. The robot's hand stands in for the carriage and a 40 mm sling for its cable. A bench analogue at 1 g; no microgravity is claimed.
setup: Station table; positions in metres, x forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up; table top z 0.7475. Boom frame R: root hinge axis at world (0.300, 0.100, 0.8375), the boom extends along -y. (1) Bus bracket, fixed: grey aluminium tower 60 x 40 x 82 mm on a 100 x 80 x 6 mm foot, gold MLI face, sRGB (0.62, 0.63, 0.66) and (0.83, 0.65, 0.22), centred (0.300, 0.125), with the root hinge cheeks at z 0.8375. (2) Boom, white-painted aluminium, sRGB (0.92, 0.92, 0.90), one articulation: root fitting and 150 x 12 x 6 mm rail (50 g) on a revolute hinge about x (torsion spring 0.9 N m/rad, rest 10 deg up, damping 0.03; stowed rest 1.2 deg down); two 14 x 16 x 10 mm dark grey root sliders (8 g each) on the rail, 120.5 mm apart stowed, driven toward each other by a self-locking left/right-hand screw (32.8 mm each, stiff drive 60,000 N/m); a lazy-tongs scissor of four 140 x 10 x 5 mm bars (130 mm pin to pin, 15 g each) in two layers and two 75 x 10 x 5 mm half bars (8 g each), 10 pins about z; at the apex a white dummy magnetometer canister 36 mm dia x 30 mm (60 g) at world (0.300, -0.042) stowed and (0.300, -0.215) at full length, canister bottom z 0.8010 when level; on it the offload sling: a grey steel bail 5 x 5 mm, 40 mm from its pin (about x, 12 mm above the apex, limits +-40 deg, light spring 0.05 N m/rad to upright) to a 36 mm axle, 10 g, and a black rubber grip sleeve 12 mm dia x 26 mm turning freely on the axle (5 g), axle at z 0.8895 upright; the bail and sleeve are the boom's only handling point. (3) Hand crank, fixed: black gearbox 40 x 40 x 50 mm (0.8 kg) at (0.300, 0.250), top z 0.8075, black crank arm (45 mm radius, 60 g) turning about z and a black rubber handle 14 mm dia x 34 mm (15 g) spinning freely on it; 11 mm of slider travel per turn, 2.98 turns stowed to full length; slip clutch at 1.5 mm. (4) Solar-cell test panel, fixed: 120 x 305 x 8 mm, blue cells sRGB (0.10, 0.18, 0.55) on an aluminium substrate (0.6 kg with legs), centred (0.300, -0.0925), top z 0.7710, on two 100 x 12 x 15.5 mm aluminium legs; 30 mm below the canister of a level boom. Friction 0.5/0.4 bars, 0.9/0.8 canister, 1.0 sleeve and crank handle. object_jitter 0: all three bodies are fixed to the table.
scoring: Every control step from the simulator reset a whole-run record (cleared only by that reset) logs the canister's lowest rim point above the cells, the root hinge angle from level, the sling's tilt from vertical (from its link pose), the tip's extension (0 stowed, 1 full) and speed, the screw, the latch, how close each gripper's fingers come to the boom (points filling the last 48 mm of both fingers, against every collider), and each gripper's pad clearance and speed. Gates, any time in the run, give 0: the canister ever within 10 mm of the cells; the root hinge ever more than 3 deg from level (drooped or pushed up); a finger ever within 5 mm of any boom part but the sling's bail and grip sleeve; the sling more than 15 deg off vertical (its grip 10.4 mm behind or ahead of its pin) on any step when a finger is within 5 mm of the sling and the tip is moving (over 2 mm/s, or the screw advancing). Then: 0 if the tip never got 50% out; 0.25 at least 50% out; 0.5 both sliders at full travel (within 0.5 mm); 0.75 latched (the latch engages only at full travel with the hinge within 2 deg of level); 1.0 latched and both grippers at least 30 mm from the boom and crank and moving under 5 mm/s for 1 s. success() is the 1.0 rung held 1 s; score() at the end otherwise.
reset_notes: Release the root latch, crank the boom fully home (2.98 turns back) so the two root sliders sit 120.5 mm apart, let the tip hang on the hinge spring (about 1.2 deg down, canister 26.7 mm above the cells) with the sling standing upright, and leave the crank handle pointing forward (+x). The bracket, gearbox and cell panel are fixed on taped outlines. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: The screw is not threads: its self-locking nut is a stiff slider drive whose target follows only the crank angle, with a 1.5 mm slip clutch. The latch is on_step logic: at full travel with the hinge within 2 deg of level it engages a 40 N m/rad brake. The root hinge spring models the boom's 1 g compliance. The 10 pins are ideal joints, 3 closing loops; bars do not collide with each other. A 40 mm bail stands in for an offload cable. Finger proximity is read from sampled finger volumes.
